entities.summary: Gaius Antistius Reginus was a Roman military officer and magistrate who played a crucial role in the Late Roman Republic and the early years of the Roman Empire. He served as a legate under the Roman general and statesman Publius Cornelius Lentulus Gaus, and later became a prominent figure in the Roman Senate. Reginus was known for his military prowess and his ability to negotiate with rival factions, earning him a reputation as a skilled diplomat and strategist. His legacy can be seen in the continued Roman dominance of the Mediterranean region during this period. The Roman historian Tacitus would later praise Reginus as a model of Roman virtues, demonstrating his enduring impact on Roman society. Reginus's contributions to the Roman Empire were instrumental in shaping the Pax Romana, a period of relative peace and stability that lasted for centuries. The Roman poet and statesman Ovid would later write about Reginus's military campaigns, highlighting his bravery and skill as a commander.
